subject: English
body: In 'He runs fast', the word 'fast' is a/an:
explanation: 'Fast' modifies the verb 'runs', so it is an adverb. In 'a fast runner' it would be an adjective.

subject: English
body: In 'She is a fast runner', the word 'fast' is a/an:
explanation: Here 'fast' describes the noun 'runner', so it is an adjective.

subject: English
body: In 'Alas! He is dead', the word 'Alas' is a/an:
explanation: An interjection expresses sudden emotion such as grief or surprise and is usually followed by an exclamation mark.

subject: English
body: In 'I will wait till you come', the word 'till' is a/an:
explanation: 'Till' joins two clauses here, so it is a conjunction. In 'till Monday' it would be a preposition.

subject: English
body: In 'The boy who came here is my brother', the word 'who' is a:
explanation: 'Who' refers back to 'the boy' and introduces a relative clause, so it is a relative pronoun.

subject: English
body: In 'Walking is good exercise', the word 'Walking' is a:
explanation: A verb + -ing used as a noun (here the subject of the sentence) is a gerund.

subject: English
body: In 'a flock of sheep', the word 'flock' is a:
explanation: A collective noun names a group as one unit: a flock of sheep, a bunch of grapes, a team of players.

subject: English
body: In 'Gold is a precious metal', the word 'Gold' is a:
explanation: Material nouns name substances, for example gold, silver, iron and wood.

subject: English
body: What is the adjective form of 'beauty'?
explanation: 'Beautiful' is the adjective, 'beautify' the verb and 'beautifully' the adverb.

subject: English
body: What is the noun form of 'brave'?
explanation: The noun of 'brave' is 'bravery'; 'bravely' is the adverb.

subject: English
body: What is the verb form of 'strong'?
explanation: 'Strength' is the noun and 'strengthen' the verb.

subject: English
body: What is the noun form of 'able'?
explanation: 'Ability' is the noun; 'enable' is a verb.

subject: English
body: What is the adjective form of 'fame'?
explanation: 'Famous' is the usual adjective of 'fame'. 'Famish' is an unrelated verb meaning to starve.

subject: English
body: What is the past participle of 'go'?
explanation: Go – went – gone.

subject: English
body: What is the past tense of 'lie' (to rest in a flat position)?
explanation: Lie (rest) – lay – lain. Lie (tell a falsehood) – lied – lied. Lay (put) – laid – laid.

subject: English
body: In 'He is too clever to be deceived', 'too' is a/an:
explanation: 'Too' modifies the adjective 'clever', and words that modify adjectives are adverbs.

subject: English
explanation: 'Ox' takes the old plural ending -en, like 'child – children'.

subject: English
explanation: Greek-origin nouns ending in -on often take -a: criterion – criteria, phenomenon – phenomena.

subject: English
explanation: Phenomenon – phenomena. 'Phenomenas' is a common mistake.

subject: English
explanation: In compound nouns the main word takes the plural: sons-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief.

subject: English
explanation: The main noun 'passer' takes the plural.

subject: English
explanation: Nouns ending in -is change to -es: analysis – analyses, crisis – crises, thesis – theses.

subject: English
explanation: Latin -us nouns often take -i: radius – radii, nucleus – nuclei, stimulus – stimuli.

subject: English
body: What is the plural of 'mouse' (the animal)?
explanation: Mouse – mice, like louse – lice.

subject: English
body: Which noun is always used in the singular and has no plural form?
explanation: Uncountable nouns such as furniture, information, advice, luggage and scenery are not used with 's'.

subject: English
body: Which noun is always plural in form and use?
explanation: Scissors, trousers, spectacles and tongs are always plural. News and subjects like mathematics take singular verbs.

subject: English
explanation: Tiger – tigress, lion – lioness.

subject: English
explanation: Drake – duck, gander – goose, cock – hen.

subject: English
explanation: A mare is a female horse; the male is a horse or stallion.

subject: English
explanation: Stag – hind (red deer). Buck – doe; ram – ewe; fox – vixen.

subject: English
explanation: Nephew – niece; uncle – aunt.

subject: English
explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an' is used.

subject: English
explanation: 'University' begins with a 'yu' consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

subject: English
explanation: 'One' begins with a 'w' sound, so 'a' is used: a one-eyed man, a one-way street.

subject: English
body: He was elected ___ MP last year.
explanation: 'MP' is read 'em-pee', starting with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

subject: English
explanation: Names of rivers, seas, oceans and mountain ranges take the definite article: the Padma, the Himalayas.

subject: English
body: I will be back in ___ hour.
explanation: The 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.

subject: English
explanation: Unique objects such as the sun, the moon and the earth take 'the'.

subject: English
body: He goes to ___ school by bus every day.
explanation: When 'school' is used for its main purpose (to study), no article is used: go to school, go to bed, go to church.

subject: English
body: Dhaka is ___ most populous city in Bangladesh.
explanation: Superlatives take 'the'.

subject: English
explanation: 'The + adjective' refers to a whole class of people: the rich, the poor, the blind.

subject: English
explanation: 'Die of' is used for diseases; 'die from' for wounds or other causes.

subject: English
explanation: Good at / bad at / clever at a subject or skill.

subject: English
explanation: 'Fond of' means liking something.

subject: English
explanation: 'Accused of' but 'charged with'.

subject: English
explanation: 'Charged with' a crime; 'accused of' a crime.

subject: English
explanation: 'Abide by' means to obey or follow.

subject: English
explanation: 'Congratulate someone on something.'

subject: English
explanation: 'Prefer A to B' — not 'than'.

subject: English
body: He is senior ___ me in service.
explanation: Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take 'to', not 'than'.

subject: English
explanation: 'Married to' someone.

subject: English
body: Divide the mangoes ___ the two brothers.
explanation: 'Between' is used for two; 'among' for more than two.

subject: English
body: He has been ill ___ last Monday.
explanation: 'Since' marks a point in time; 'for' marks a period (for three days).

subject: English
body: He has been absent ___ three days.
explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time.

subject: English
explanation: 'Comply with' a rule or order.

subject: English
explanation: 'Jealous of' someone.

subject: English
body: He is not aware ___ the danger.
explanation: 'Aware of' something.

subject: English
explanation: 'Translate into' a language, which shows change of state.

subject: English
explanation: 'Different from' is the standard form in formal English.

subject: English
explanation: 'Blind of one eye' but 'deaf to advice'.

subject: English
body: The teacher was angry ___ the student.
explanation: 'Angry with' a person; 'angry at' a thing or situation.

subject: English
explanation: 'Abstain from' means to keep away from.

subject: English
explanation: 'Averse to' means opposed to or unwilling.

subject: English
body: Nothing can prevent him ___ going there.
explanation: 'Prevent someone from doing something.'

subject: English
explanation: 'Dispense with' means to do without.

subject: English
explanation: 'Indifferent to' means showing no interest in.

subject: English
explanation: 'On time' means punctually; 'in time' means early enough.

subject: English
explanation: 'Insist on' + noun or gerund.

subject: English
explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on, used with 'since', takes the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
explanation: 'Yesterday' is a definite past time, so the simple past is used, not the present perfect.

subject: English
body: By next year, she ___ her degree.
explanation: 'By + a future time' calls for the future perfect.

subject: English
body: The train ___ before we reached the station.
explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect.

subject: English
explanation: Universal truths are expressed in the simple present.

subject: English
body: It is high time we ___ the work.
explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the simple past (subjunctive use).

subject: English
explanation: 'Look!' signals an action happening now, so the present continuous is used.

subject: English
body: He ___ for two hours when I arrived.
explanation: An action that continued for a period up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

subject: English
body: No sooner had he arrived ___ it started raining.
explanation: 'No sooner … than' is a fixed pair.

subject: English
body: Hardly had he left ___ the guests arrived.
explanation: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when' is the correct pair, not 'than'.

subject: English
explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it takes a gerund.

subject: English
explanation: 'Be used to' (accustomed to) takes a gerund; 'used to + base verb' describes a past habit.

subject: English
explanation: 'Mind' is followed by a gerund.

subject: English
body: The teacher made us ___ the poem again.
explanation: 'Make, let, have' (causative) are followed by the bare infinitive.

subject: English
body: While I was reading, the light ___ off.
explanation: A short action interrupting a longer past action takes the simple past.

subject: English
explanation: 'Since 2020' links the past to now, so the present perfect is used.

subject: English
body: I ___ the novel by the time the film was released.
explanation: 'By the time + past' calls for the past perfect in the main clause.

subject: English
body: One of the boys ___ absent today.
explanation: The subject is 'one', so the verb is singular.

subject: English
body: Each of the students ___ a book.
explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb.

subject: English
explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' (meaning many) takes a plural verb.

subject: English
explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb.

subject: English
body: Bread and butter ___ my favourite breakfast.
explanation: Two nouns forming one idea or dish take a singular verb.

subject: English
explanation: Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) take a singular verb.

subject: English
body: The cattle ___ grazing in the field.
explanation: 'Cattle' is always plural.

subject: English
body: Either you or he ___ responsible for this.
explanation: With 'either … or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('he').

subject: English
body: The teacher, along with his students, ___ going on a tour.
explanation: Phrases such as 'along with', 'as well as' and 'together with' do not change the subject; 'the teacher' is singular.

subject: English
body: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
explanation: An amount of distance, money or time considered as one whole takes a singular verb.

subject: English
body: Many a man ___ died in this war.
explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.

subject: English
body: Neither of the two answers ___ correct.
explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb in formal English.

subject: English
explanation: 'News' looks plural but is an uncountable singular noun.

subject: English
body: The jury ___ divided in their opinions.
explanation: A collective noun takes a plural verb when its members act individually, as "divided in their opinions" shows.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'He writes a letter.'
options: A letter was written by him.
A letter is written by him.
A letter is being written by him.
A letter has been written by him.
explanation: Simple present active becomes "am/is/are + past participle".

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'She is singing a song.'
options: A song is sung by her.
A song is being sung by her.
A song was being sung by her.
A song has been sung by her.
explanation: Present continuous becomes "is/are being + past participle".

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'Open the door.'
explanation: Imperative sentences become "Let + object + be + past participle".

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'They have finished the work.'
options: The work has been finished by them.
The work had been finished by them.
The work was finished by them.
The work is finished by them.
explanation: Present perfect becomes "has/have been + past participle".

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'Who broke the glass?'
options: By whom the glass was broken?
By whom was the glass broken?
Whom was the glass broken by him?
explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom', followed by question word order.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'I know him.'
options: He has been known by me.
explanation: 'Know' takes the preposition 'to' in the passive.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'The news surprised me.'
options: I am surprised at the news.
I was surprising at the news.
I was surprised at the news.
The news was surprised by me.
explanation: 'Surprised' commonly takes 'at' in the passive; the tense stays simple past.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'People speak English all over the world.'
options: English was spoken all over the world.
English is spoken all over the world.
English is being spoke all over the world.
English has spoken all over the world.
explanation: When the agent is general (people, someone), it is usually dropped in the passive.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'Somebody has stolen my pen.'
options: My pen was stolen by somebody.
explanation: Present perfect → 'has been + past participle'; the indefinite agent is dropped.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'Do it at once.'
options: Let it be done at once.
explanation: Imperative → 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

subject: English
body: Choose the passive form: 'He will do the work.'
options: The work will be done by him.
The work would be done by him.
The work will been done by him.
The work is done by him.
explanation: Future simple → 'will be + past participle'.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said, "I am ill."
options: He told that he was ill.
He said that I am ill.
He said that he is ill.
He said that he was ill.
explanation: With a past reporting verb, present tense shifts to past and pronouns change to match the speaker.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: She said to me, "Are you happy?"
options: She asked me if I am happy.
She asked me if I was happy.
She said to me if I was happy.
She asked me was I happy.
explanation: Yes/no questions use 'asked + if/whether' and normal word order.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where I live.
He said me where I lived.
explanation: Wh-questions keep the question word but use statement word order and shift the tense back.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun."
options: The teacher told that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
explanation: Universal truths keep the present tense in indirect speech.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said to me, "Please help me."
options: He requested me to help him.
He told me that please help him.
He asked me that I help him.
He requested me to help me.
explanation: Requests become 'requested + object + to-infinitive'.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said, "I will go tomorrow."
options: He said that he would go tomorrow.
He said that he will go tomorrow.
He said that he would go the next day.
He said that I would go the next day.
explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said to me, "Don't go there."
options: He told me that do not go there.
He told me to not go here.
He said me not go there.
He told me not to go there.
explanation: Negative commands become 'told/forbade + object + not to + verb'; 'there' stays.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said, "Let us go home."
options: He said that let them go home.
He told them to let us go home.
He proposed that they should go home.
He proposed that we will go home.
explanation: 'Let us' (a suggestion) becomes 'proposed/suggested that … should'.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: She said, "Alas! I am undone."
options: She said alas that she was undone.
She exclaimed with sorrow that she was undone.
She exclaimed that alas she is undone.
She told with sorrow that I was undone.
explanation: Exclamations drop the interjection and use 'exclaimed with sorrow/joy that'.

subject: English
body: Choose the indirect form: He said, "I have done it."
options: He said that he had done it.
He said that he has done it.
He said that he did it.
He said that I had done it.
explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect.

subject: English
body: If I were rich, I ___ a car.
explanation: An imaginary present situation (second conditional) uses past tense + would + base verb.

subject: English
body: If he had worked hard, he ___.
explanation: An imaginary past situation (third conditional) uses had + past participle with would have + past participle.

subject: English
body: Unless you work hard, you ___ fail.
explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and takes the first-conditional pattern. Never use 'not' after 'unless'.

subject: English
body: ___ I known about it, I would have helped you.
explanation: Inversion 'Had I known' replaces 'If I had known'.

subject: English
body: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
explanation: 'Were' is used for all persons in imaginary conditions.

subject: English
explanation: After 'wish', an unreal present takes 'were'.

subject: English
body: He talks as if he ___ the owner of the company.
explanation: 'As if' for an unreal situation is followed by 'were'.

subject: English
body: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
explanation: A real future possibility takes the first conditional: present + will.

subject: English
body: Choose the comparative form: 'He is the tallest boy in the class.'
options: No boy is as tall as him in the class only.
He is taller than all boy in the class.
He is more tall than any boy.
He is taller than any other boy in the class.
explanation: A superlative becomes 'comparative + than any other + singular noun'.

subject: English
body: Choose the positive form: 'He is the best player in the team.'
options: He is as good as other players.
No player is as best as he.
No other player in the team is as good as he.
No other player is better as he.
explanation: 'No other … as + positive adjective + as' expresses the superlative in the positive degree.

subject: English
body: Choose the superlative form: 'Very few cities in Bangladesh are as big as Dhaka.'
options: Dhaka is the biggest city in Bangladesh.
Dhaka is one of the biggest cities in Bangladesh.
Dhaka is bigger than all cities.
Dhaka is one of the bigger city in Bangladesh.
explanation: 'Very few … as … as' becomes 'one of the + superlative + plural noun'.

subject: English
body: Transform: 'As soon as he came, I left.'
options: No sooner had he come than I left.
No sooner did he come when I left.
No sooner he came than I left.
Hardly had he come than I left.
explanation: 'As soon as' becomes 'No sooner had … than'.

subject: English
body: Transform: 'He is too weak to walk.'
options: He is very weak to walk.
He is so weak that he can walk.
He is so weak that he cannot walk.
He is too weak that he cannot walk.
explanation: 'Too … to' becomes 'so … that … cannot'.

subject: English
body: Which of the following is a complex sentence?
options: I know that he is honest.
He is poor but he is honest.
In spite of his poverty, he is honest.
Work hard and you will succeed.
explanation: A complex sentence has one main clause and at least one subordinate clause ('that he is honest').

subject: English
body: Which of the following is a compound sentence?
options: I know that he is poor.
Though he is poor, he is honest.
He is poor but he is honest.
explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction ('but').

subject: English
body: 'What a beautiful bird it is!' is a/an ___ sentence.
explanation: An exclamatory sentence expresses strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.

subject: English
body: 'May you live long!' is a/an ___ sentence.
explanation: An optative sentence expresses a wish or prayer.

subject: English
body: Transform into a simple sentence: 'Though he was ill, he attended the meeting.'
options: Although ill, but he attended the meeting.
He was ill but he attended the meeting.
He was ill, so he attended the meeting.
In spite of his illness, he attended the meeting.
explanation: 'Though + clause' becomes 'In spite of + noun phrase'.

subject: English
explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary.

subject: English
explanation: 'Let's' always takes 'shall we'.

subject: English
explanation: The negative tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I'.

subject: English
explanation: 'Nobody' makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive and uses 'they'.

subject: English
explanation: Imperatives usually take 'will you' / 'won't you'.

subject: English
explanation: 'Seldom', 'hardly' and 'never' are negative in meaning, so the tag is positive.

subject: English
explanation: 'Everyone' takes 'they' in the tag.

subject: English
explanation: 'Ought to' expresses moral duty or obligation.

subject: English
body: He ___ swim when he was five.
explanation: 'Could' expresses ability in the past.

subject: English
body: You ___ have told me earlier; I would have helped you.
explanation: 'Should have + past participle' expresses something that was advisable but not done.

subject: English
options: He is more senior than me.
explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to', not 'than'.

subject: English
options: I live here for five years.
I have been living here since five years.
I am living here since five years.
I have been living here for five years.
explanation: 'For' with a period of time and the present perfect continuous.

subject: English
options: He gave me a piece of advice.
explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable; use 'a piece of advice'.

subject: English
options: One of my friends are a doctor.
One of my friend is a doctor.
One of my friends is a doctor.
One of my friend are a doctor.
explanation: 'One of' + plural noun + singular verb.

subject: English
options: She is cleverest than her sister.
She is more cleverer than her sister.
She is most cleverer than her sister.
She is cleverer than her sister.
explanation: Double comparatives ('more cleverer') are wrong.

subject: English
options: I am hear a strange noise.
I am hearing a strange noise.
explanation: Verbs of perception such as 'hear' are normally not used in the continuous form.

subject: English
options: He returned back to home late.
explanation: 'Return' already means 'come back', so 'back' is redundant; 'home' takes no preposition here.

subject: English
explanation: 'Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition.

subject: English
options: The police is arresting the thief yesterday.
The police has arrested the thief.
The police have arrested the thief.
The polices have arrested the thief.
explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun.

subject: English
options: He is one of the best players in the team.
He is one of the best player in the team.
He is one of the better player in the team.
He is one the best players in team.
explanation: 'One of the + superlative + plural noun'.

subject: English
explanation: After 'let', object pronouns are used: him and me.

subject: English
options: Between you and I, he is not trustworthy.
Between you and me, he is not trustworthy.
Between you and myself, he is not trustworthy.
Between I and you, he is not trustworthy.
explanation: Prepositions take object pronouns: between you and me.

subject: English
options: The sceneries of Cox's Bazar are beautiful.
The scenery of Cox's Bazar is beautiful.
The scenery of Cox's Bazar are beautiful.
The sceneries of Cox's Bazar is beautiful.
explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

subject: English
explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time like 'yesterday'.

subject: English
options: Unless you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you will work hard, you will fail.
Unless you worked hard, you will fail.
explanation: 'Unless' already contains 'not'; adding another negative is a double negative.

subject: English
options: Though he is poor, yet but he is honest.
Though he is poor but he is honest.
Though he is poor, he is honest.
Although he is poor but honest he is.
explanation: 'Though' and 'but' should not be used together in the same sentence.

subject: English
options: The man which car was stolen called the police.
The man who's car was stolen called the police.
The man whom car was stolen called the police.
The man whose car was stolen called the police.
explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun; 'who's' means 'who is'.

subject: English
options: Scarcely he had gone when the phone rang.
Scarcely had he gone than the phone rang.
Scarcely had he gone when the phone rang.
Scarcely did he gone when the phone rang.
explanation: 'Scarcely' at the start requires inversion ('had he gone') and pairs with 'when'.

subject: English
explanation: Present perfect uses 'has/have + past participle (gone)'.

subject: English
options: The furniture in this room is expensive.
The furnitures in this room are expensive.
The furniture in this room are expensive.
The furnitures in this room is expensive.
explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and singular.

subject: English
options: Hardly had I reached the station than the train left.
Hardly I had reached the station when the train left.
Hardly had I reached the station when the train left.
Hardly did I reached the station when the train left.
explanation: 'Hardly' at the beginning requires inversion and pairs with 'when'.

subject: English
body: The ___ of the school delivered a speech.
explanation: 'Principal' means the head of an institution or main; 'principle' means a rule or belief.

subject: English
body: He bought some ___ such as pens and paper.
explanation: 'Stationery' (with -ery) means writing materials; 'stationary' (with -ary) means not moving.

subject: English
body: The bus remained ___ for an hour.
explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving.

subject: English
body: The loud noise did not ___ his concentration.
explanation: 'Affect' is usually a verb (to influence); 'effect' is usually a noun (a result).

subject: English
body: The new law will come into ___ next month.
explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start to apply.

subject: English
body: I ___ you to see a doctor.
explanation: 'Advise' (with s) is the verb; 'advice' (with c) is the noun.

subject: English
explanation: 'Lose' means to fail to keep; 'loose' means not tight.

subject: English
body: All the students ___ Rahim were present.
explanation: 'Except' means apart from; 'accept' means to receive.

subject: English
explanation: 'Accept' means to receive or agree to.

subject: English
body: Her ___ to the problem was very practical.
explanation: 'Approach' means a way of dealing with something; 'reproach' means blame.

subject: English
body: The judge must be ___, favouring neither side.
explanation: 'Disinterested' means impartial; 'uninterested' means not interested.

subject: English
body: The doctor gave him an ___ for the pain.
explanation: An anodyne is a painkiller; an antidote counteracts a poison; an anecdote is a short story.

subject: English
explanation: To abandon is to leave behind or forsake.

subject: English
